title: WinoGen: A Highly Configurable Winograd Convolution IP Generator for Efficient CNN Acceleration on FPGA
problem: Building efficient and highly compatible IP cores for arbitrary Winograd convolution operations on FPGA remains underexplored. Existing implementations lack the flexibility to handle arbitrary input/output tile sizes and kernel sizes while maintaining high performance.
motivation: Winograd convolution can effectively improve computation performance and save hardware resources in FPGA-based CNN accelerators, making efficient and flexible IP generation critical for practical deployment.
method: The paper proposes Structured Direct Winograd Convolution (SDW), a novel reformulation of Winograd convolution enabling efficient hardware implementation. WinoGen is a Chisel-based IP generator that accepts arbitrary input/output tile sizes and kernel sizes as parameters, automatically generating optimized hardware implementations. The generated IP maintains compatibility with multiple kernel and tile size configurations.
key_novelty: Structured Direct Winograd Convolution (SDW) reformulation enables automatic generation of configurable Winograd convolution hardware that supports multiple kernel sizes and tile sizes while maintaining high efficiency.
contributions: Novel Structured Direct Winograd (SDW) convolution reformulation for efficient FPGA implementation
WinoGen: a Chisel-based configurable Winograd convolution IP generator for arbitrary tile and kernel sizes
Automatic generation of optimized high-performance IP cores compatible with multiple configurations
Demonstrated 2.45×-3.10× performance improvements over state-of-the-art CNN accelerators
primary_theme: Winograd convolution IP generation for FPGA CNN acceleration
